exposure: State COVID-19 prevalence (high vs. national average)
outcome: Universal laboratory testing for COVID-19 admissions
Personal protective equipment (PPE) recommendations for vaginal and cesarean deliveries
cohort: 301 Labor and delivery (L&D) units in the United States
finding: Universal laboratory testing for COVID-19 was more common in academic institutions and states with high disease prevalence, while N95 mask use during asymptomatic vaginal deliveries was less likely in hospitals with universal testing.
mod_finding: When delivering asymptomatic patients, full PPE (including N95 mask) was recommended for vaginal deliveries in 33% and for cesarean delivery in 38% of responding institutions.
